_what: An independent web check of every claim extracted into nsgp-data.json, run 2026-08-08 before the deadline table shipped.
_why_separate: nsgp-data.json is a mechanical extraction of NPSA's grant-knowledge Drive folder and says so: re-extract when Drive changes rather than editing by hand. Folding these corrections into it would break that — the next extraction would silently revert them, and a hand-edit would be indistinguishable from Drive content. So this is an overlay applied on top, and every row the tool renders carries the layer it came from.
_method: Each dated row, each administering agency, and each state program's caps and eligibility was searched against the administering agency's own published material. Where a date and its stated day-of-week were both available, the pair was checked for consistency — that alone caught one bad date.
_evidence_limit: The sandbox's egress proxy refused direct page fetches to every .gov host and to the third-party grant aggregators, so this is search-derived rather than read off the agency's page. That is weaker evidence. It is strong enough to correct a date that two independent results agree on and that passes the day-of-week check, and strong enough to withdraw a 'confirmed' claim nothing corroborates. It is NOT strong enough to invent a date, so nothing here is added on a single weak hit.

corrections.why: Texas collects NSGP subapplications through eGrants months ahead of the rest of the country — the FFY2026 solicitation closed February 12, 2026, with awards performing from September 1, 2026. The extracted date put it in July alongside everyone else. A Texas client told 'you have until July' misses the cycle by five months, and there is no second window.
sources: grantedai.com — Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP), Federal Fiscal Year 2026, Office of the Governor, State of Texas
